- Remove all references to the skchr gh account in the readme and anywhere elese in the codebase and  use the prjctimg acc
- Clean up the @AGENTS.md file  so that it remains concise and doesn't unnecessarily pollute our context with over specific info which sometimes we don't need as we are working
- Delete all tags 0.7.x and resume the version 0.6.118 as the latest tag and adjust the version bumping logic to increment the last part of the patch since the current approach was moving too fast towards 1.x

<type>file</type>
<content>
1: - Read exact versioned docs at <https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v55.0.0/> before writing any code.
2: - **Never run `npm install` on the dev machine.** Only edit `package.json` to add/change dependencies. The user handles installation separately.
3: - After editing `package.json`, update `AGENTS.md` if the change introduces new conventions or build steps.
4: - Run `npm run check-exercises` after editing `src/data/courses/*.yaml`. It asserts each task's validation rules are consistent with the exercise's `solution` (final task state) and that `expectedPixels`/`pixelMatch` rules are well-formed.
5: - Validation rule model (see `src/data/types.ts`): `functionCall`, `functionExists`, `canvasSize`, `pixelMatch` (single strict point), `expectedPixels` (multi-point, passes if matching fraction >= `minPassFraction`, default 0.9). The exercise-level `solution` represents the FINAL task's target state.
6: 
7: ## Course modules (YAML → TS build artifacts)
8: 
9: - **Source of truth: `src/data/courses/*.yaml`** — edit YAML, never the `.ts` files.
10: - `scripts/build-courses.mjs` reads every `.yaml` in `src/data/courses/` and emits a matching `.ts` next to it (`<slug>Course` export).
11: - `build-courses` runs automatically via `postinstall` (so a fresh clone is buildable) and via `npm start` (so local edits propagate). CI's release workflow relies on `postinstall` during `npm install` — it does not re-run `build-courses` itself.
12: - **`src/data/courses/*.ts` are gitignored build artifacts** (see `.gitignore`, same convention as `src/data/reference.generated.json`). Never commit them.
13: - After editing any `.yaml`, re-run `npm run build-courses` before type-checking or starting the app.
14: 
15: ## p5.js bundling (always latest)
16: 
17: - `scripts/bundle-p5.mjs` queries the npm registry for the latest `p5` release, downloads `lib/p5.min.js`, and regenerates `src/utils/p5Source.ts` (the vendored minified source as `const _p = [...]; export const p5Source = _p.join("")`) plus `src/utils/p5Version.ts` (`export const p5Version = "X.Y.Z"`).
18: - `bundle-p5` runs first in `postinstall` (before `gen-reference`) and first in `npm start`, so the app always bundles the newest p5.js. `scripts/generate-reference.mjs` reads the version stamp from `src/utils/p5Version.ts` instead of hardcoding it.
19: - **`src/utils/p5Source.ts` and `src/utils/p5Version.ts` are gitignored build artifacts** — never commit them. A fresh clone regenerates them on `npm install`.
20: 
21: ## Release cadence
22: 
23: - **Every push to `main` must bump the app version and create a matching git tag.** This is enforced by a `pre-push` git hook (`scripts/hooks/pre-push`, repo tracks `core.hooksPath = scripts/hooks`).
24: - To bump atomically, run `sh scripts/bump-version.sh <X.Y.Z>` — it updates `app.json` (`expo.version`) and `package.json` (`version`) together.
25: - Workflow: edit → `sh scripts/bump-version.sh 0.6.10X` → `git add -A` → `git commit -m "v0.6.10X: <subject>"` → `git tag vX.Y.Z` → `git push origin main && git push origin vX.Y.Z`.
26: - Patch bumps (`0.6.10X`) for bug fixes / small UX changes; minor bumps (`0.7.0`) for new features; major bumps for breaking changes. The hook refuses a `main` push if the pushed commit range doesn't include a version bump in `package.json` or if the matching `vX.Y.Z` tag doesn't exist locally.
27: 
28: ## Loop Engineering
29: 
30: This repo uses loop engineering patterns. See:
31: - `.opencode/STATE.md` — current loop memory
32: - `.opencode/LOOP.md` — active loops and cadence
33: - `.opencode/loop-budget.md` — token caps
34: - `.opencode/loop-constraints.md` — binding agent rules
35: - `.opencode/loop-run-log.md` — run history
36: - `.opencode/gate.yaml` — path denylist + auto-merge allowlist
37: - `.opencode/skills/` — triage and verifier skills
38: 
39: Start a loop: `opencode run "Run loop-triage. Update .opencode/STATE.md."`
40: Verify changes: `opencode run "Verify diff in worktree" --agent verifier`

(End of file - total 40 lines)
</content>

#!/bin/sh
set -e

# Usage: ./scripts/bump-version.sh <version>
# Example: ./scripts/bump-version.sh 0.6.56
#
# Updates version in:
#   - app.json (expo.version)
#   - package.json (version)

VERSION="$1"

if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 <version>"
  echo "Example: $0 0.6.56"
  exit 1
fi

# Validate version format (semver-like: X.Y.Z)
if ! echo "$VERSION" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$'; then
  echo "Error: Version must be in semver format (e.g., 0.6.56)"
  exit 1
fi

echo "Bumping version to $VERSION..."

# Update app.json
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const app = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('app.json', 'utf8'));
app.expo.version = '$VERSION';
fs.writeFileSync('app.json', JSON.stringify(app, null, 2) + '\n');
console.log('  Updated app.json');
"

# Update package.json
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const pkg = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('package.json', 'utf8'));
pkg.version = '$VERSION';
fs.writeFileSync('package.json', JSON.stringify(pkg, null, 2) + '\n');
console.log('  Updated package.json');
"

echo "Version bumped to $VERSION"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pre-push git hook (see AGENTS.md "Release cadence").
# Refuses a push to main unless the pushed commit range includes a version bump
# in package.json AND a matching vX.Y.Z tag exists locally.
#
# Reads stdin: <local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha> per line.

set -e

while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha; do
  # Only enforce on the main branch.
  if [[ "$local_ref" != "refs/heads/main" ]]; then
    continue
  fi

  # Resolve the range of commits being pushed.
  if [[ -z "$remote_sha" || "$remote_sha" == "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ]]; then
    range="$local_sha"
  else
    range="$remote_sha..$local_sha"
  fi

  repo_dir="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

  # Detect a version bump in package.json within the pushed range.
  bumped_version=""
  if git diff --name-only "$range" -- "$repo_dir/package.json" 2>/dev/null | grep -q package.json; then
    bumped_version=$(git show "$local_sha:package.json" 2>/dev/null | node -e "
      let data='';
      process.stdin.on('data',c=>data+=c);
      process.stdin.on('end',()=>{
        try { process.stdout.write(JSON.parse(data).version || ''); }
        catch(e) { process.stdout.write(''); }
      });
    ")
  fi

  if [[ -z "$bumped_version" ]]; then
    echo "[pre-push] ERROR: push to main must include a version bump in package.json." >&2
    echo "           Run: sh scripts/bump-version.sh <X.Y.Z>  then commit, then:" >&2
    echo "           git tag vX.Y.Z  before pushing." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  # Confirm the matching tag exists locally.
  if ! git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$bumped_version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "[pre-push] ERROR: package.json is at $bumped_version but tag v$bumped_version does not exist locally." >&2
    echo "           Run: git tag v$bumped_version  before pushing." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

exit 0

## What is this ?

Learn P5 is a mobile app to help users learn how p5.js symbols (functions, classes, built-in variables) work by showing users their sketch preview during the exercise. It is not a replacement for the p5 web editor which has far more comprehensive editing features.

This is a [GSoC 2026](https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/programs/2026/projects/wmrV9qBT) project for the [Processing Foundation](https://processingfoundation.org).

## Who is this for ?

This app is intended for anyone who wants to learn p5.js at a relaxed pace that covers how each symbol works on the go, even without an internet connection to load resources such as the reference or web editor.

## How can I try it out ?

The app is currently available on Android only and ChromeOS if you are on the `dev` branch.

            npm install && NPM_INSTALLED=true && echo "npm install succeeded" && break
            echo "npm install failed (attempt $i)"
            if [ $i -lt 3 ]; then sleep 10; fi
          done
          if [ "$NPM_INSTALLED" != "true" ]; then
            echo "Failed to install npm dependencies after 3 attempts"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Regenerate CodeMirror bundle
        run: npm run bundle-editor

      - name: Setup JDK
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: 17

      - name: Setup Android SDK
        uses: android-actions/setup-android@v3

      - name: Install NDK
        run: |
          NDK_INSTALLED=false
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            echo "Attempt $i to install NDK 27.1.12297006..."
            yes | $ANDROID_SDK_ROOT/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager \
              --install "ndk;27.1.12297006" || { echo "SDK manager failed"; sleep 10; continue; }
            NDK_DIR="$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT/ndk/27.1.12297006"
            if [ -d "$NDK_DIR" ]; then
              echo "NDK installed successfully at $NDK_DIR"
              NDK_INSTALLED=true
              break
            fi
            echo "NDK directory not found, retrying..."
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$NDK_INSTALLED" != "true" ]; then
            echo "Failed to install NDK after 3 attempts"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Prebuild native project
        run: |
          PREBUILT=false
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            echo "Attempt $i to prebuild native project..."
            npx expo prebuild --platform android --clean && PREBUILT=true && break
            echo "prebuild failed (attempt $i)"
            if [ $i -lt 3 ]; then sleep 10; fi
          done
          if [ "$PREBUILT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "Failed to prebuild native project after 3 attempts"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Configure ABI splits for per-architecture APKs
        run: |
          sed -i '/android {/a\
          \    splits {\
          \        abi {\
          \            enable true\
          \            reset()\
          \            include "arm64-v8a", "armeabi-v7a"\
          \            universalApk false\
          \        }\
          \    }' android/app/build.gradle

      - name: Build release APKs (per ABI)
        run: cd android && ./gradlew assembleRelease

      - name: List split APKs
        run: find android -name "*.apk" -type f

      - name: Rename APKs to learn-p5-{tag}-{arch}-debug.apk
        run: |
          for apk in android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/*.apk; do
            dir=$(dirname "$apk")
            base=$(basename "$apk")
            arch=$(echo "$base" | sed -n 's/.*\(arm64-v8a\|armeabi-v7a\).*/\1/p')
            [ -z "$arch" ] && arch=universal
            mv "$apk" "$dir/learn-p5-${{ github.ref_name }}-$arch-debug.apk"
          done

      - name: Upload split APKs to release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/*.apk

--- .husky/pre-push	
+++ .husky/pre-push	
@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env sh
+# Pre-push hook (Husky).
+# 1) Push Entire CLI session logs alongside the user's push.
+# 2) Enforce that a push to main includes a version bump in package.json
+#    AND a matching vX.Y.Z tag (see AGENTS.md "Release cadence").
+
+# 1) Entire CLI session-log hook (no-op if the CLI is unavailable).
+if command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  entire hooks git pre-push "$1" || true
+fi
+
+# 2) Version-bump enforcement.
+while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha; do
+  [ "$local_ref" = "refs/heads/main" ] || continue
+
+  if [ -z "$remote_sha" ] || [ "$remote_sha" = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ]; then
+    range="$local_sha"
+  else
+    range="$remote_sha..$local_sha"
+  fi
+
+  repo_dir=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
+
+  bumped_version=""
+  if git diff --name-only "$range" -- "$repo_dir/package.json" 2>/dev/null | grep -q package.json; then
+    bumped_version=$(git show "$local_sha:package.json" 2>/dev/null | node -e "
+      let data='';
+      process.stdin.on('data',c=>data+=c);
+      process.stdin.on('end',()=>{
+        try { process.stdout.write(JSON.parse(data).version || ''); }
+        catch(e) { process.stdout.write(''); }
+      });
+    ")
+  fi
+
+  if [ -z "$bumped_version" ]; then
+    echo "[pre-push] ERROR: push to main must include a version bump in package.json." >&2
+    echo "           Run: sh scripts/bump-version.sh  then commit, then:" >&2
+    echo "           git tag v0.6.<next>  before pushing." >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+
+  if ! git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$bumped_version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "[pre-push] ERROR: package.json is at $bumped_version but tag v$bumped_version does not exist locally." >&2
+    echo "           Run: git tag v$bumped_version  before pushing." >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+done
+
+exit 0

input.content:
#!/bin/sh
set -e

# Bump the app version in app.json (expo.version) and package.json (version).
#
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/bump-version.sh          # auto-increment the patch (0.6.118 -> 0.6.119)
#   ./scripts/bump-version.sh <X.Y.Z>  # override with an explicit version

VERSION="$1"

if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
  CURRENT=$(node -e "process.stdout.write(require('./package.json').version)")
  if ! echo "$CURRENT" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$'; then
    echo "Error: current version '$CURRENT' is not semver; pass an explicit <X.Y.Z>" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  VERSION=$(echo "$CURRENT" | awk -F. '{printf "%d.%d.%d", $1, $2, $3+1}')
  echo "Auto-incrementing patch: $CURRENT -> $VERSION"
fi

if ! echo "$VERSION" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$'; then
  echo "Error: version must be in semver format (e.g., 0.6.118)"
  exit 1
fi

echo "Bumping version to $VERSION..."

# Update app.json
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const app = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('app.json', 'utf8'));
app.expo.version = '$VERSION';
fs.writeFileSync('app.json', JSON.stringify(app, null, 2) + '\n');
console.log('  Updated app.json');
"

# Update package.json
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const pkg = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('package.json', 'utf8'));
pkg.version = '$VERSION';
fs.writeFileSync('package.json', JSON.stringify(pkg, null, 2) + '\n');
console.log('  Updated package.json');
"

echo "Version bumped to $VERSION"

>

An offline first mobile app to help users learn p5.js through small (bite sized 🍣) exercises. It is not a replacement for the p5 web editor which has far more comprehensive editing features.

This is a [GSoC 2026](https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/programs/2026/projects/wmrV9qBT) project for the [Processing Foundation](https://processingfoundation.org).

## What is this ?

Learn P5 is a mobile app to help users learn how p5.js symbols (functions, classes, built-in variables) work by showing users their sketch preview during the exercise. It is not a replacement for the p5 web editor which has far more comprehensive editing features.

This is a [GSoC 2026](https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/programs/2026/projects/wmrV9qBT) project for the [Processing Foundation](https://processingfoundation.org).

## Who is this for ?

This app is intended for anyone who wants to learn p5.js at a relaxed pace that covers how each symbol works on the go, even without an internet connection to load resources such as the reference or web editor.

## How can I try it out ?

The app is currently available on Android only and ChromeOS if you are on the `dev` branch.

You can [grab the latest release here](https://github.com/skchr/learn-p5/releases/tag/latest)

## Where can I see and share suggestions ?

There's a few GitHub Discussions that are open to suggestions and where we post feature previews (screenshots and the like).

>

An offline first mobile app to help users learn p5.js through small (bite sized 🍣) exercises. It is not a replacement for the p5 web editor which has far more comprehensive editing features.

This is a [GSoC 2026](https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/programs/2026/projects/wmrV9qBT) project for the [Processing Foundation](https://processingfoundation.org).

## What is this ?

Learn P5 is a mobile app to help users learn how p5.js symbols (functions, classes, built-in variables) work by showing users their sketch preview during the exercise. It is not a replacement for the p5 web editor which has far more comprehensive editing features.

This is a [GSoC 2026](https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/programs/2026/projects/wmrV9qBT) project for the [Processing Foundation](https://processingfoundation.org).

## Who is this for ?

This app is intended for anyone who wants to learn p5.js at a relaxed pace that covers how each symbol works on the go, even without an internet connection to load resources such as the reference or web editor.

## How can I try it out ?

The app is currently available on Android only and ChromeOS if you are on the `dev` branch.

You can [grab the latest release here](https://github.com/skchr/learn-p5/releases/tag/latest)

## Where can I see and share suggestions ?

There's a few GitHub Discussions that are open to suggestions and where we post feature previews (screenshots and the like).

More threads will be created as the project progresses:

- [Accessibility](https://github.com/skchr/learn-p5/discussions/1)

## Roadmap & Project Status

**See [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) for a comprehensive, up-to-date feature tracker** with implementation status (✅ Done, 🟡 Partial, ⬜ Planned) across all areas: onboarding, courses, exercises, reference, dashboard, gamification, editor, keyboard, offline architecture, settings, notifications, accessibility, playground, minigames, and more.

The ROADMAP.md is the single source of truth for what's implemented and what's coming next.

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# Pre-push hook (Husky).
# 1) Push Entire CLI session logs alongside the user's push.
# 2) Enforce that a push to main includes a version bump in package.json
#    AND a matching vX.Y.Z tag (see AGENTS.md "Release cadence").

# 1) Entire CLI session-log hook (no-op if the CLI is unavailable).
if command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  entire hooks git pre-push "$1" || true
fi

# 2) Version-bump enforcement.
while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha; do
  [ "$local_ref" = "refs/heads/main" ] || continue

  if [ -z "$remote_sha" ] || [ "$remote_sha" = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ]; then
    range="$local_sha"
  else
    range="$remote_sha..$local_sha"
  fi

  repo_dir=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)

  bumped_version=""
  if git diff --name-only "$range" -- "$repo_dir/package.json" 2>/dev/null | grep -q package.json; then
    bumped_version=$(git show "$local_sha:package.json" 2>/dev/null | node -e "
      let data='';
      process.stdin.on('data',c=>data+=c);
      process.stdin.on('end',()=>{
        try { process.stdout.write(JSON.parse(data).version || ''); }
